nodes.description: Biallelic CTU2 variants remove the scaffold subunit of the cytosolic tRNA thiouridylase. CTU2 does not catalyse the thiolation itself - CTU1 does - but the activity belongs to the CTU1-CTU2 complex, and CTU2 loss abolishes it. Most reported alleles are protein-truncating, including the founder splice variant c.873G>A, which destroys a donor site despite leaving the codon unchanged.

nodes.description: The developmental pattern - small brain with cortical and callosal malformation, absent or malformed kidney, under-masculinised external genitalia, heart defects and limb anomalies - points to a defect during organogenesis. Why these organs are affected, and not others, is unexplained. Knockdown of the partner subunit ctu1 in zebrafish impairs angiogenesis and embryonic development, and is the nearest vertebrate model; no CTU2 animal model has been reported. HYPOTHETICAL because the link from the tRNA defect to any specific organ malformation has not been studied.

nodes.description: The 2-thio group restricts wobble pairing and strengthens codon-anticodon interaction for the split codon boxes read by these three tRNAs. In fission yeast and nematodes, loss of Ctu1-Ctu2 causes misreading and frameshifting, genome instability and abnormal development, and over-expressing the hypomodified tRNAs suppresses the yeast defects. PROVISIONAL because no study has measured translation in CTU2-deficient human cells or tissues; the original authors name translational efficiency and fidelity as the candidate mechanism, not a demonstrated one.

nodes.description: The wobble uridine of cytosolic tRNA-Lys(UUU), tRNA-Glu(UUC) and tRNA-Gln(UUG) normally carries mcm5s2U: a 5-methoxycarbonylmethyl group added by Elongator and ALKBH8, and a 2-thio group added by CTU1-CTU2. Cells from patients with each tested CTU2 allele, including the founder allele, lack the 2-thio group on all thiol-containing tRNAs.
